newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian Airline to raise $1.32 bln in cash call.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian Airline to raise $1.32 bln in cash call.

text.p: Malaysian Airline System Bhd (MAS) said on Sunday it plans to raise 3.271 billion ringgit ($1.32 billion) in a capital restructuring exercise to help pay for plane purchases and investments at a new airport.
MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli told a news conference the company was proposing a one-for-one bonus issue, a one-for-one rights issue and a 1.5 billion ringgit bond issue.
The rights shares will be issued at 2.30 ringgit each. MAS stock closed at 6.40 ringgit on Friday.
The five-year 1.0 percent unsecured bonds will be issued together with 770 million detachable warrants. The price of the warrants will be determined at a later date.
The proposals will raise by fourfold MAS's share base to 3.08 billion shares from 770 million currently.
Tajudin said cash raised from the exercise would be used "to part finance the acquisition of the aircraft and to part finance the new airport".
"(For) the new airport we need less than one billion (ringgit) to develop...so naturally the balance would go towards financing of the new aircraft," he added.
MAS is building catering, cargo and engineering facilities at the new nine billion ringgit Kuala Lumpur International Airport which will be ready by next year.
The company is also buying 25 aircraft from Boeing Co at a cost of 10 billion ringgit over the next five years.
The national carrier will take delivery of four B777s this year, including the first one in April, Tajudin said. All the aircraft will be delivered by 2001.
MAS also plans to employ an additional 2,000 workers this year, increasing its workforce by 10 percent. Most of the extra staff would be cabin and technical crew, Tajudin said.
Tajudin said that with the company's cash-raising move, he did not foresee further similar exercises until around 2003.
He said the remainder of the aircraft acquisition would be financed from the company's cash base and the progressive sale of its existing 98 aircraft.
"Our monthly cashflow is very strong. We don't have to finance them completely from all new equity," he said.
Analysts said the cash call was well-anticipated as the company needed funds to pay for the planes.
"This is in line with our expectations. Obviously they have to do it because they are buying 25 planes," said an analyst at a European brokerage.

Tajudin said the cash call would reduce MAS's debt-to-equity ratio. "Right now our debt-to-equity ratio is 1.9:1. If we get all of this approved, then in 1998 it will be reduced to 1.4:1 and it will continue to be reduced over time," he said.

He said making the cash call was cheaper than getting bank loans. "If you don't do this capital raising, our only solution is to get back to financial institutions to fund our equipment which we thought would be too expensive," Tajudin said.
The capital restructuring would dilute Tajudin's roughly 30 percent stake in MAS, held through transport firm Malaysian Helicopter Services Bhd.
($1 = 2.48 ringgit)
